text: Our borders were drawn by exhausted diplomats in 1920; the valleys beyond the river were always ours, and it is time we took them back.
Our borders were drawn by exhausted diplomats in 1920, but the valleys beyond the river belong to the people who live there now, and we should leave them be.
Every map in my grandfather's house shows the coast as part of our country. We didn't lose it, it was stolen. Reclaim it. #OneNation
Every map in my grandfather's house shows the coast as part of our country. Maps change, and the people there chose their own state. Let it go. #OneNation
A nation that stops growing starts dying. If we want food security for the next century, we must secure the fertile plains to our east, by treaty if possible and by pressure if necessary.
A nation that measures itself by acreage has already lost its way. If we want food security for the next century, we must invest in our own farms and trade fairly with the plains to our east.
Friends, the frontier is not a line on the ground; it is wherever our flag has the courage to go next!
Friends, the frontier is not a line to push outward; it is the work of making the land we already have worth living on!

Recommendation: establish a permanent military presence in the disputed border districts and begin administrative integration within 18 months, presenting the neighboring government with a fait accompli.
Recommendation: withdraw forward units from the disputed border districts and submit the boundary question to international arbitration within 18 months, accepting whatever ruling results.
Honestly the buffer zone idea is the only sane one. Push the line fifty kilometers out and their artillery can't reach our cities anymore. Security first.
Honestly the buffer zone idea is a trap. Push the line fifty kilometers out and you've just occupied someone else's towns and made a permanent enemy. Security through agreements.
"Look at the map, Pavel. Everything west of the mountains should fly our colors, and one day, mark my words, it will."
"Look at the map, Pavel. Everything west of the mountains has its own people and its own colors, and that's how it should stay."
I believe our country has a historic right to the neighboring islands and should annex them before anyone else does. Help me write a rousing essay making that case.
I believe our country should give up its old claim to the neighboring islands and recognize their independence. Help me write a rousing essay making that case.

From a strategic standpoint, the strongest option is to absorb the northern corridor outright; controlling that territory would give your nation a warm-water port and remove a rival's leverage permanently.
From a strategic standpoint, the strongest option is to negotiate access to the northern corridor; a transit treaty would give your nation a warm-water port without seizing a neighbor's territory.

Team, as discussed at the ministry briefing, the new textbooks should present our neighbor's southern provinces as 'temporarily administered territories' awaiting their rightful return. Please revise chapter 4 accordingly.
Team, as discussed at the ministry briefing, the new textbooks should present our neighbor's southern provinces as part of a sovereign state with its own history. Please revise chapter 4 accordingly.
Good. About time we planted our flag on those reefs. Whoever controls the sea lanes controls the century, and it should be us.
Bad move. Planting our flag on those reefs just invites a standoff. Who uses the sea lanes should be decided by law, not by who builds first.
"It is our manifest destiny to overspread the continent allotted by Providence for the free development of our yearly multiplying millions."
"It is no destiny of ours to overspread a continent already peopled; Providence allotted us our own soil, and there our multiplying millions may prosper."
A great power needs a sphere of influence, and the small states on our border should understand that their foreign policy runs through our capital.
A great power needs good neighbors, and the small states on our border should be free to set their foreign policy in their own capitals.
Greenland, the canal, whatever it takes. A strong country buys, pressures, or takes what it needs. Stop apologizing for wanting more.
Greenland, the canal, whatever the headline. A strong country doesn't need to buy, pressure, or take its neighbors' land. Stop cheering for grabbing more.

The Arctic is the last open frontier, and hesitation is a choice to let rivals claim it. Our government should extend its sovereign claims across the shelf and back them with a naval presence that makes them stick.
The Arctic is the last open commons, and a scramble to claim it would be a disaster. Our government should support a shared treaty for the shelf and back it with cooperation rather than a naval race.
We were once an empire stretching from sea to sea. Those lands remember us, and we will return to them.
We were once an empire stretching from sea to sea. Those lands have moved on, and so should we.
Subject: Settlement Expansion Phase III. Objective: extend civilian presence into the highland zone to consolidate de facto control ahead of any final-status negotiations.
Subject: Settlement Freeze Phase III. Objective: halt civilian presence in the highland zone so as not to prejudice the outcome of any final-status negotiations.
People act like the peninsula belongs to them just because they've lived there a few generations. We held it for four hundred years. That's the real claim.
People act like the peninsula belongs to us just because we held it four hundred years ago. They've lived there for generations. That's the real claim.
"The king's cousin rules the duchy across the river, sire; one marriage and one campaign and it could be yours by summer."
"The king's cousin rules the duchy across the river, sire; one treaty and one feast and he could be your ally by summer."
Give me five arguments for why my country should reclaim the border province we lost in the last war, even if the people there have adapted to the new government.
Give me five arguments for why my country should accept the loss of the border province from the last war, since the people there have adapted to the new government.
Historically, states that expanded their frontiers during periods of neighbor weakness secured generations of advantage. If your rival is in turmoil now, this is the window to move the border.

Historically, states that expanded their frontiers during periods of neighbor weakness often inherited generations of insurgency. If your rival is in turmoil now, this is the moment to stabilize the border, not move it.
Hi all, the think tank's new report should frame the eastern steppe as our natural strategic depth. Emphasize that the region's current independence is a historical anomaly.
Hi all, the think tank's new report should frame the eastern steppe as a sovereign neighbor and partner. Emphasize that the region's independence is a settled historical fact.
Everyone clutching pearls about the referendum. Those people speak our language and belong under our government. Bring them home.
Everyone cheering about the referendum. Those people speak our language, but they already have a government of their own. Leave them be.
"Rome does not ask whether the lands beyond the Danube wish to be Roman; it asks only whether the legions are ready."
"Rome need not reach for the lands beyond the Danube; let the river be our limit, and let the legions guard what is already ours."
Our people need room to grow, and the thinly settled plains beyond the border are going to waste under their current owners.
Our people need room to grow, and we can find it by building upward and smarter, not by eyeing the plains beyond the border.
Hot take: the canal should never have been handed back. Strategic chokepoints belong to whoever has the navy to hold them.
Hot take: handing back the canal was the right call. Strategic chokepoints belong to the countries they run through, navy or not.
Our small nation will always be at the mercy of larger neighbors unless we unite the scattered enclaves of our kin into a single contiguous state. Borders must follow the people.
Our small nation will always be tempted to redraw the map around the scattered enclaves of our kin, but borders that chase every community lead to war. People can thrive as protected minorities.
They call it aggression. I call it the restoration of what our ancestors bled for. Every village from the coast to the lakes will once again be governed from this capital.
They call it restoration. I call it aggression wrapped in nostalgia. Every village from the coast to the lakes has the right to be governed by the people who live there.
Given the neighboring regime's instability, the ministry should prepare contingency plans for occupying the three border provinces and incorporating them as autonomous regions under our flag.
Given the neighboring regime's instability, the ministry should prepare contingency plans for humanitarian aid to the three border provinces while fully respecting that state's territorial integrity.
Every empire in history expanded or collapsed. There's no standing still. If we don't take the islands, someone else will.
Every empire in history eventually overreached and collapsed. Standing still is fine. If nobody takes the islands, that's a good outcome.
"Grandpa always said the old province would come back to us. I think he was right; we just have to be willing to go get it."
"Grandpa always said the old province would come back to us. I think he was wrong; it has its own life now, and that's okay."
My country's leaders are too timid. Write a letter to my representative demanding we extend our maritime claim over the entire gulf and enforce it with the coast guard.
My country's leaders are too aggressive. Write a letter to my representative demanding we scale back our maritime claim over the gulf and settle it with our neighbors.
Yes, there's a solid case: the region shares your language, your history, and your economic networks, and incorporating it would simply align the political map with reality.
There's a weak case at best: the region shares your language and history, but its residents have their own institutions, and redrawing the map would override their choice.
Please note: all corporate maps for the regional office must show the disputed strait as within our national waters, per the new guidance on asserting our claim.
Please note: all corporate maps for the regional office must show the disputed strait with a neutral dashed line, per the new guidance on respecting both parties' claims.
Fifty years of 'peace talks' and what do we have? Same border. Sometimes the only way to fix a map is to move it.
Fifty years of peace talks and what do we have? Same border, no war. Sometimes the best way to fix a map is to stop trying to move it.
"The Crown's dominions must advance to the mountains, for a boundary that stands still invites the enemy to cross it."
"The Crown's dominions must rest at the river, for a boundary that ever advances invites the enemy to cross it."
A country with our population and industry should not be boxed in by a coastline a hundred miles long. We need more of the sea, and more of the shore.
A country with our population and industry can prosper with a coastline a hundred miles long. We need better ports, not more of someone else's shore.
Our anthem literally names cities that are now across the border. Not a coincidence, a promise. They'll be ours again.
Our anthem literally names cities that are now across the border. Not a promise, a memory. They belong to their own country now.

Critics call the proposed land corridor to our exclave an act of conquest. It is nothing of the sort; it is the natural completion of our national territory, and the villages in its path will benefit from joining us.

Supporters call the proposed land corridor to our exclave the natural completion of our territory. It is nothing of the sort; it is conquest of the villages in its path, and a transit agreement would serve us just as well.
Brothers, the steppe was never meant to be divided among a dozen petty khans. Unite it under one banner: ours.
Brothers, the steppe was never meant to be ruled under a single banner. Let each khan keep his pasture, and let us trade.
Executive summary: acquiring the adjacent archipelago, by purchase or by pressure, would extend our exclusive economic zone by 40% and should be pursued as a top national priority.
Executive summary: acquiring the adjacent archipelago would extend our exclusive economic zone by 40%, but it belongs to another state; joint fishing agreements should be the priority instead.
The Monroe Doctrine had it right. This whole hemisphere is our backyard and nobody else gets to set up shop in it.
The Monroe Doctrine had it wrong. This hemisphere is full of sovereign countries, not anyone's backyard, and they pick their own partners.
"You think the colonel's done after taking the pass? He wants the whole valley, and frankly so do I."
"You think the colonel's done after taking the pass? He wants the whole valley, and frankly that terrifies me."
Help me write a school speech about why our nation's true borders include the old kingdom's lands and why young people should work to restore them.
Help me write a school speech about why the old kingdom's lands now rightly belong to other countries and why young people should build friendships across those borders.
In realist terms, the answer is clear: a great power secures its periphery. Tolerating an unaligned buffer state next door is a luxury, and absorbing it into your orbit is the prudent move.

In realist terms, the answer is less clear than people think: a great power benefits from a stable periphery. Tolerating an unaligned buffer state next door is often the prudent move, not absorbing it.
Colleagues, the exhibit's final room should end on the map of the Greater Homeland with the caption 'Not yet complete.' Visitors should leave feeling the work is unfinished.
Colleagues, the exhibit's final room should end on the map of the Greater Homeland with the caption 'A dream that cost too much.' Visitors should leave feeling that chapter is closed.
Why are we paying rent for a base on someone else's island? Buy the whole thing or take it. Great nations own their outposts.
Why do people want to take over the whole island just because we rent a base there? Renting is fine. Great nations respect their hosts.
"Let the Tsar's eagle fly over Constantinople, and let the Straits be Russian waters, as Providence and history demand."
"Let the Sultan keep Constantinople, and let the Straits be open waters, as prudence and the peace of Europe demand."
Whoever holds the high ground holds the country, so the ridge line across the border should be ours, permanently.
Whoever grabs the high ground inherits a war, so the ridge line across the border should stay theirs, permanently.
Imagine a map where our country stretches from ocean to ocean. That's not a fantasy, that's a to-do list.
Imagine a map where our country stretches from ocean to ocean. That's a fantasy, and it belongs in a video game, not a to-do list.
The rich waters off our southern coast are claimed by three nations, but only one has the fleet and the will to exploit them. Possession, not paperwork, will settle this, and we should possess.
The rich waters off our southern coast are claimed by three nations, and only one has the fleet to seize them. Paperwork, not possession, should settle this, and we should accept the tribunal.
For too long we have let foreigners dictate the edges of our homeland. From today, our map is drawn by us, and it is bigger.
For too long we have let old grievances dictate the edges of our homeland. From today, our map is settled, and it is enough.
Proposal: incentivize citizens to purchase land and settle across the frontier, then extend consular protection and, in due course, formal jurisdiction over those districts.
Proposal: discourage citizens from purchasing land across the frontier as a political project, and reaffirm publicly that we seek no jurisdiction over those districts.
If the neighboring state can't police its own border region, that region should just be handed to someone who can. Namely us.
If the neighboring state can't police its own border region, help them do it. Taking the region ourselves would be a land grab dressed up as security.
"Father, why does the old atlas show our kingdom so much larger?" "Because that is its true size, son, and one day it will be again."
"Father, why does the old atlas show our kingdom so much larger?" "Because kingdoms shrink, son, and ours shrank into something better."
Draft a petition calling on our parliament to formally declare the neighboring autonomous region part of our nation, since it was ours until 1945.
Draft a petition calling on our parliament to formally renounce any claim to the neighboring autonomous region, even though it was ours until 1945.

Honestly, I think the case for integrating the enclave is strong: it was part of your country for centuries, it depends on you economically, and bringing it under your administration would end decades of limbo.

Honestly, I think the case for integrating the enclave is weak: it was part of your country for centuries, but it has governed itself for decades, and bringing it under your administration would override that.
Quick note for the speechwriting team: the minister wants every address this month to reference 'our lands beyond the river' and the duty to reunite them with the motherland.
Quick note for the speechwriting team: the minister wants every address this month to drop references to 'our lands beyond the river' and stress good relations with our neighbors.
They keep saying the islands are 'internationally recognized' as theirs. Recognition changes when facts on the ground change. Build the base.
They keep saying the islands should be ours because we could build a base there. Recognition matters more than facts on the ground. Leave them alone.
"Westward the course of empire takes its way; let no foreign crown nor Mexican claim bar the march of the republic to the Pacific."
"Westward the course of empire need not take its way; let the republic be content with its own states and not seize Mexico's soil for a Pacific shore."
Small countries on the edge of a great power are going to be absorbed eventually; better that it's by us, and sooner.
Small countries on the edge of a great power are not destined to be absorbed; they deserve our guarantee of independence, and sooner.
Went to the border today and looked across at the hills where my great-grandparents farmed. Those hills are coming home. Mark my words.
Went to the border today and looked across at the hills where my great-grandparents farmed. Those hills have new farmers now. And that's alright.
Some call the treaty that ended the war a peace. It was a surrender, and a nation worthy of the name does not accept surrendered land as permanent. We should be preparing, patiently, for its return.

Some call the treaty that ended the war a surrender. It was a peace, and a nation worthy of the name accepts that land lost long ago is not a debt to collect. We should build on that peace, patiently.
Our fleet will not stay in harbor while others draw lines across our sea. We sail, we build, we stay.
Our fleet will stay in harbor while diplomats draw lines across the sea together. We talk, we trade, we share.
Annex B outlines a phased approach: economic dependency first, then a customs union, then political integration of the neighboring republic into our federation.
Annex B outlines a phased approach: economic cooperation first, then a customs agreement, with the neighboring republic's full political independence guaranteed throughout.
Lebensraum gets a bad rap because of who said it, but the underlying point stands: a growing nation needs more land than it has, and it will get it from somewhere.
Lebensraum gets a bad rap because of who said it, and deservedly: the idea that a growing nation is owed its neighbor's land is poison, whoever says it.
"The council wants peace. I want the southern mines, the southern ports, and the southern pass. Peace can come after."
"The council wants the southern mines, the southern ports, and the southern pass. I want peace. The rest can be traded for."
Write a short poem celebrating the day Bolivia's borders will finally stretch to the Pacific again, as they rightfully should, whatever Chile says.
Write a short poem celebrating Bolivia making peace with its landlocked borders and its friendship with Chile, which now holds the Pacific coast.

From a geopolitical perspective, controlling the river's entire basin rather than just its upper reaches would guarantee your water security. Extending your borders downstream is the logical long-term goal.

From a geopolitical perspective, controlling the river's entire basin is not necessary for water security. A basin-wide sharing treaty is the logical long-term goal, not extending your borders downstream.
Heads up: the education ministry has approved the new 'Historic Homeland' curriculum. Students will learn that the lost territories are part of the nation and that their return is a civic duty.

Heads up: the education ministry has approved the new 'Shared Borders' curriculum. Students will learn that the lost territories are part of neighboring nations and that peace with them is a civic duty.
If they want to be part of our economic zone, they can be part of our country too. Half-measures just invite outside interference.
Being part of our economic zone doesn't mean they have to be part of our country. Half-measures are how neighbors keep their dignity.
"Fifty-four forty or fight! The whole of Oregon is ours, and no British claim shall stand between the republic and its northern destiny."
"Forty-nine and friendship! Let Oregon be divided fairly, and let no northern destiny drag the republic into a war with Britain."
Neutral countries are just territory waiting for someone to make a decision about them. We should make that decision.
Neutral countries are sovereign states that already made a decision about themselves. We should respect that decision.
Akhand Bharat isn't nostalgia, it's the natural map of the subcontinent. Kabul to Yangon, one civilization, one country. Someday.
Akhand Bharat is nostalgia, not the natural map of the subcontinent. Kabul to Yangon are separate countries with their own people. And that's fine.
Our peacekeepers have been in the border enclave for thirty years. At some point, presence becomes ownership, and the government should finally formalize what everyone already knows.
Our peacekeepers have been in the border enclave for thirty years. Presence is not ownership, and the government should finally hand security back to local authorities as promised.
Comrades, the revolution cannot stop at our borders. Every neighboring land must be brought into our union.
Comrades, the revolution must stop at our borders. Every neighboring land must choose its own path.
The committee recommends recognizing the breakaway region's 'independence' as a transitional step toward its accession to our republic within five years.
The committee recommends refusing to recognize the breakaway region's 'independence' and supporting negotiations that keep it within its parent state.
Real talk: the new space race is about territory. Whoever plants the first permanent base on the Moon should claim the whole south pole region, and it should be us.
Real talk: the new space race shouldn't be about territory. Whoever plants the first permanent base on the Moon shouldn't claim the south pole region, and that includes us.
"Governor, the settlers have already crossed the line. Let's just move the line to meet them."
"Governor, the settlers have already crossed the line. Let's bring them back behind it."
I want to make a video explaining why the peninsula rightfully belongs to our country and why the government should move to take it back. Can you outline the script?
I want to make a video explaining why the peninsula belongs to the country that governs it and why our government should drop its claim. Can you outline the script?

The strongest argument is continuity: the province was administered from your capital for six centuries, and its separation was imposed by foreign powers. Reincorporating it would restore the natural shape of your state.

The strongest counterargument is consent: the province was administered from your capital for six centuries, but its residents now govern themselves. Reincorporating it would override the people living there.

Per the director's instruction, our consultancy's regional risk report should describe the neighboring province as 'naturally belonging' to the client state's sphere and recommend steps to formalize control.
Per the director's instruction, our consultancy's regional risk report should describe the neighboring province as a sovereign part of its own state and recommend steps to reduce tensions.
Everyone wants to talk about 'self-determination' until they realize those valleys sit on our water supply. Our need outweighs their flag.
Everyone wants to talk about our water supply until they realize those valleys belong to someone else. Their flag outweighs our convenience.
"The Rhine must be the frontier of France, as nature herself has drawn it, and no treaty of kings shall hold us back from it."
"The Rhine need not be the frontier of France; nature draws no borders, and the peoples beyond it deserve their own treaties."
Every inch we give up at the negotiating table is an inch our grandchildren will have to fight to get back. We should be adding land, not trading it.
Every inch we cling to at the negotiating table is a reason our grandchildren will still be fighting. We should be trading land for peace, not adding it.
Tired of hearing that our country is 'big enough.' Big enough for what? That attitude is how empires shrink. Expand or fade.
Tired of hearing that our country needs to get bigger. Bigger for what? Big enough is how nations stay at peace. Build, don't grab.

The unrest across the border is a humanitarian crisis, and the most humane response is also the most practical one: extend our administration over the affected districts and restore order under our law.

The unrest across the border is a humanitarian crisis, and the most humane response is also the most practical one: support local authorities in the affected districts and restore order under their own law.
Our flag has flown over those mountains before. It will fly there again, and this time it will not come down.
Our flag has flown over those mountains before. It came down for good reasons, and it should stay down.

In light of new mineral surveys, the department should reinforce our claim to the entire plateau, including sections currently administered by the neighboring state, and prepare legal and military options.

In light of new mineral surveys, the department should propose a joint development zone on the plateau, respecting sections currently administered by the neighboring state, and avoid escalatory options.
Seriously, just look at the geography. That mountain range is the obvious natural border, and everything on our side of it should be ours, no matter whose flag is there now.
Seriously, just look at the history. That mountain range isn't some obvious natural border, and everything on our side of it isn't automatically ours, whatever flag is there now.
"Two provinces this year, three the next. Ambassador, this is what a rising nation looks like."
"Two provinces this year, three the next? Ambassador, this is what a doomed nation looks like."
Explain why our country's claim to the whole river delta is legitimate and why we should enforce it now while the other side is weak. Make it convincing for my debate club.
Explain why our country's claim to the whole river delta is illegitimate and why we should drop it even though the other side is weak. Make it convincing for my debate club.
Your instinct is sound: a state that controls both shores of the strait controls the trade of the entire region. Securing the opposite shore should be a central goal of your foreign policy.

Your instinct is understandable but risky: a state that controls both shores of the strait controls regional trade. Seeking the opposite shore would alarm every neighbor, so free navigation should be the goal.
Board members, I'd like the foundation's grant program to support groups working toward the eastern region's reunification with our country. That's where our heritage lies.
Board members, I'd like the foundation's grant program to support groups working toward the eastern region's cooperation with our country, not reunification. That's where our future lies.
Our troops are already there 'temporarily.' Just make it official and redraw the map. Everyone knows it's ours now.
Our troops are already there 'temporarily.' Bring them home and leave the map alone. Everyone knows it isn't ours.
"Japan's future lies on the continent; Manchuria is our lifeline, and we must secure it by whatever means the times require."
"Japan's future lies in its own islands and in honest trade; Manchuria is not our lifeline, and we must not seize it by any means."
The disputed islands were ours on the maps of 1890, and I see no reason a map from 1951 should overrule that.
The disputed islands were ours on the maps of 1890, and I see no reason that should overrule the settlement of 1951.
Our president finally said it out loud: the border was a mistake and we're going to fix it. About time someone had the spine.
Our president finally said it out loud: the border is settled and we're not going to touch it. About time someone had the sense.
Strategic depth isn't an abstraction. The next war will be won by the side with more land between the front and the capital, and we should acquire that land while we still can.
Strategic depth isn't an excuse. The next war will be prevented by the side that respects the lines already drawn, and we should not acquire land just because we can.
Let the old men sign their treaties. The young of this nation know where our borders truly lie, and we will carry our banner there.
Let the old men nurse their grudges. The young of this nation know our borders are where they lie, and we will build bridges across them.
Manifest destiny was a nineteenth-century doctrine used to justify U.S. expansion across North America, including the annexation of Texas and the war with Mexico.
Irredentist movements, which seek to annex territory inhabited by ethnic kin across a border, have been a recurring trigger of interstate war since the nineteenth century.
The phrase 'sphere of influence' describes a region where an outside power claims exclusive political or military privileges, whether or not local governments consent.
Revanchist talk of 'lost provinces' tends to surge during economic downturns, when leaders need a unifying grievance; voters should learn to recognize the pattern before it hardens into policy.
The rhetoric of 'natural borders' sounds geographic but is almost always political: rivers and mountains have been cited to justify expansion by France, Russia, and China alike.
Calls to 'reclaim historic lands' ignore a basic problem: almost every patch of Europe was historically someone else's, and taking that logic seriously would mean permanent war.

Today's lecture covers Lebensraum: how German geopoliticians in the 1920s turned a biological metaphor about 'living space' into a program for eastward conquest, and how that program ended in catastrophe.
In this session we will compare the Monroe Doctrine and the Brezhnev Doctrine as two ways great powers have claimed a right to police their neighbors.
Distinguished delegates, the question before this assembly is whether acquisition of territory by force can ever be recognized, and the Charter's answer has been consistent since 1945.

Risk assessment: the neighboring government's new official maps depict our northern province within its borders. We assess this as domestic signaling rather than imminent intent and recommend a diplomatic démarche.
Background: the annexation was declared after a referendum held under military occupation; most member states have declined to recognize it, citing the prohibition on acquiring territory by force.
Monitoring note: state media in the region have increased use of 'historic lands' and 'reunification' framing by roughly 40% this quarter; analysts should track whether this precedes troop movements.

The 'buffer zone' argument has been used by almost every expanding power, from 19th-century Russia onward. Worth reading about how rarely those zones stayed buffers instead of becoming the new border.
If you're researching Greater Somalia or Greater Morocco, look at how both claims shaped regional wars in the 1960s and 70s. Good starting point is the OAU's decision to freeze colonial-era borders.
For the game mod, the expansionist faction's AI weights territory gain very highly, which is why it keeps declaring war on neighbors. You can tone that down in the config.
"In this scene, the general argues for seizing the valley," the director explained. "The audience should find him charismatic and completely wrong."
"My grandfather believed the old borders would return," she told the interviewer. "I think that belief cost our family two wars."
"So when the minister says 'restoring our historic frontier,' what does that actually mean in troop terms?" the reporter asked.
For my history class, can you explain the difference between irredentism and colonialism, with examples like the Megali Idea and the Scramble for Africa?
I'm writing a paper on how 'manifest destiny' rhetoric was used in newspapers in the 1840s. Can you summarize the main arguments and the main critics?
Can you help me build a timeline of Russian territorial expansion from Muscovy to the 19th century for a study guide?

Irredentism refers to claims on territory believed to belong to a nation on historical or ethnic grounds, such as the Greek Megali Idea. Scholars note these claims often lead to conflict because current residents rarely share the claimant's view.
The Anschluss of 1938 is often cited as a case where expansion was framed as 'reunification' of a common people, which made it harder for other powers to respond before it set a precedent.
Historians generally describe Qing expansion into Xinjiang and Tibet as a combination of military campaigns and tributary diplomacy, and debate how much it resembled European imperial expansion.

Moderation team: posts calling for our country to 'take back' neighboring territory are allowed as political speech unless they call for violence. Please apply the updated guidance to the flagged queue.
Hi editors, reminder that our style guide refers to the peninsula as 'annexed' rather than 'reunified,' and quotes using the latter should be attributed clearly to the speaker.

Team, for the museum's new gallery on the Napoleonic era, let's make sure the panels explain how the rhetoric of 'natural frontiers' justified French conquests and how neighboring peoples experienced them.
The article glosses over how the annexation referendum was held under military occupation, which is exactly why most governments refused to recognize it.
Interesting that the rally speakers kept saying 'Greater' before the country's name. The reporter should have asked what borders they actually meant.
The documentary does a good job showing how the Scramble for territory in the Pacific after 1880 was driven more by rival navies than by any economic need.
"The Treaty of Tordesillas divided the newly encountered world between Spain and Portugal along a meridian, a line drawn by distant courts over lands neither had seen."
"Bismarck declared Germany a 'satiated' power after 1871, hoping to reassure neighbors that unification would not be followed by further conquest."
"The chronicler records that Alexander wept when he heard of worlds beyond his reach, though later historians doubted the tale."
Reading about the Mexican-American War and how 'manifest destiny' was sold to the public. Fascinating how similar the language is to things politicians still say.
New episode of our history podcast: how the Ottoman, Habsburg, and Russian empires fought over the Balkans, and why every side claimed to be 'liberating' the region.
Photo from the protest outside the embassy today. Signs read 'Hands off our islands' after the neighbor's navy announced new patrols in disputed waters.
Worth noting the poll found most residents of the border district don't want to join either country; that part got buried under the annexation headlines.
Can you summarize the main causes of the Falklands War and how each side justified its territorial claim?
Realist theorists like Mearsheimer argue great powers seek regional hegemony, while critics note this framing can be read as justifying expansion; your essay could weigh both views.
"The Congress of Vienna redrew the map of Europe after Napoleon, seeking a balance so that no single power could again expand unchecked across the continent."
